privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.contact: If you have any questions about this privacy policy, please contact us:
privacy.section1Content: BudgetWise ("we", "our", "us") is committed to protecting the privacy of our users. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store, and protect your personal information when you use the BudgetWise application (the "Application"). This policy is designed to comply with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25).
privacy.section2Content:
We collect the following types of personal information:

• Account information: email address, name, and encrypted password.
• Financial data: bank account details, transaction history, account balances, and budget information obtained through your connected financial institutions via the Plaid service.
• Usage data: application preferences, consent records, and audit logs of account activity.
• Authentication data: session tokens and two-factor authentication configuration.

We only collect information that is necessary for the operation of the Application.
privacy.section3Content:
We collect your information through:

• Direct input: when you create an account and configure your settings.
• Plaid integration: when you connect your bank accounts, financial data is retrieved through Plaid's secure API. Plaid's own privacy policy governs their data handling practices.
• Automatic collection: session and audit data generated through your use of the Application.

We obtain your explicit consent before collecting, using, or disclosing your personal information. You may withdraw consent at any time through the Privacy & Consent settings.
privacy.section4Content:
Your personal information is used for the following purposes:

• Providing the Application's core features: displaying your financial accounts, transactions, budgets, and reports.
• Authentication and security: verifying your identity and protecting your account.
• Categorization: automatically and manually organizing your transactions.
• Data export: allowing you to export your financial data in CSV or JSON format.

We do not use your information for advertising, marketing to third parties, or any purpose beyond operating the Application.
privacy.section5Content:
Your data is stored in a secure database with the following protections:

• Passwords are hashed using industry-standard algorithms and are never stored in plain text.
• Authentication tokens are cryptographically generated and have defined expiration periods.
• Two-factor authentication (TOTP) is available for additional account security.
• Access to the database is restricted and protected by server-level security measures.
• Data is isolated per user — you can only access your own data.

We retain your data only for as long as necessary to provide the Application's services or as required by law.
privacy.section6Content:
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties.

Your financial data is shared with Plaid Technologies, Inc. solely for the purpose of connecting to your financial institutions. No other third-party sharing occurs.

We may disclose your information if required by law, court order, or governmental regulation.
privacy.section7Content:
Under PIPEDA and Quebec Law 25, you have the following rights:

• Right of access: You may request access to the personal information we hold about you.
• Right of rectification: You may request correction of inaccurate information.
• Right of deletion: You may request the deletion of your personal data. The Application provides a secure data deletion feature in Settings that permanently removes all your financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and rules).
• Right to withdraw consent: You may withdraw your consent for data collection, processing, or storage at any time through the Privacy & Consent settings. Withdrawal of certain consents may limit your ability to use specific features.
• Right to data portability: You may export your data at any time using the built-in export feature.
• Right to file a complaint: You may file a complaint with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec.
privacy.section8Content:
The Application implements a granular consent management system:

• Cookie consent: You may accept or decline cookies when first accessing the Application.
• Data collection consent: Controls whether the Application can connect to and synchronize data from your bank accounts.
• Data processing consent: Controls whether the Application can process your data for dashboard and reporting features.
• Data storage consent: Controls whether the Application stores your financial data. Revoking storage consent triggers a secure deletion process.

You can manage all consent preferences at any time in the Privacy & Consent section of Settings.
privacy.section9Content:
In the event of a data breach that poses a real risk of significant harm, we will:

• Notify affected users as soon as feasible.
• Notify the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
• Notify the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec.
• Keep a record of the breach as required by law.
privacy.section10Content:
For any questions, concerns, or requests regarding your personal information, you may contact our Privacy Officer:

BudgetWise
1234 rue de l'Église, Lévis (QC) H0H0H0
Email: budgetwise@guisset.ca

We will respond to your request within 30 days, as required by law.
privacy.section11Content: The Application is not intended for use by individuals under the age of 14. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we become aware that a child under 14 has provided us with personal information, we will take steps to delete that information.
privacy.section12Content: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Any changes will be reflected in the "Last updated" date at the top of this policy. We encourage you to review this policy periodically. Continued use of the Application after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

securityPolicy.title: Information Security Policy
securityPolicy.contact: For questions regarding this Information Security Policy, please contact:
securityPolicy.section1Content:
BudgetWise is committed to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all information assets entrusted to us by our users. This Information Security Policy (ISP) establishes the framework for our information security program and defines the principles, responsibilities, and standards that govern how we protect sensitive data.

Our objectives are to:

• Protect user financial data and personal information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
• Ensure the availability and reliability of the BudgetWise application and its supporting infrastructure.
• Comply with applicable laws and regulations, including PIPEDA and Quebec's Law 25.
• Maintain user trust through transparent and responsible data handling practices.
• Continuously improve our security posture through regular reviews and updates.
securityPolicy.section2Content:
This policy applies to:

• All information assets managed by the BudgetWise application, including user account data, financial transaction records, bank connection credentials, budget configurations, and audit logs.
• All technical infrastructure supporting the application, including web servers, databases, APIs, and third-party integrations (e.g., Plaid).
• All individuals with access to BudgetWise systems, including administrators and end users.
• All environments: production, staging, and development.

This policy covers data at rest, data in transit, and data in processing within the BudgetWise ecosystem.
securityPolicy.section3Content:
Clear accountability is essential to an effective security program. The following roles and responsibilities are established:

• Application Owner / Administrator: Responsible for the overall security of the BudgetWise application, including maintaining this policy, managing user access, monitoring the audit log, and responding to security incidents. Administrators have elevated privileges and are accountable for their responsible use.
• Users: Responsible for maintaining the security of their own credentials, enabling two-factor authentication when possible, and reporting any suspicious activity. Users must not share their login credentials or authentication tokens.
• Third-Party Providers (Plaid): Subject to their own security policies and contractual obligations. BudgetWise selects third-party providers that maintain appropriate security standards and certifications.

All security responsibilities are documented and reviewed during each policy update cycle.
securityPolicy.section4Content:
BudgetWise implements robust authentication and access control measures:

• Password Security: All passwords are hashed using industry-standard bcrypt algorithms. Passwords are never stored in plain text. Users are encouraged to use strong, unique passwords.
• Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): Optional TOTP-based two-factor authentication is available for all users. 2FA adds a second layer of verification using a time-based one-time password generated by an authenticator app. One-time recovery codes are provided during 2FA setup.
• Session Management: Authentication tokens are cryptographically generated, stored securely, and have defined expiration periods. Sessions are invalidated upon logout.
• Role-Based Access: Administrative functions (user management, Plaid configuration, audit log review) are restricted to users with the administrator role. Standard users can only access their own data.
• Audit Logging: All authentication events (successful logins, failed attempts, 2FA changes, password changes) are recorded in the audit log with timestamps, IP addresses, and user agent information.
securityPolicy.section5Content:
BudgetWise employs multiple layers of data protection:

• Data Isolation: Each user's data is logically isolated. API endpoints enforce user-scoped queries, ensuring users can only access their own financial data.
• Encryption in Transit: All communications between the user's browser and the BudgetWise server are encrypted using TLS (HTTPS).
• Database Security: Access to the database is restricted to the application layer. Direct database access is not available to end users.
• Sensitive Data Handling: Plaid access tokens and API credentials are stored securely and are never exposed to the client-side application.
• Data Minimization: We only collect and retain data necessary for the application's functionality. No data is collected for advertising or third-party marketing purposes.
securityPolicy.section6Content:
In the event of a security incident, BudgetWise follows a structured response process:

• Detection: Security events are monitored through the audit log system. Unusual patterns (e.g., repeated failed login attempts, unauthorized access attempts) are flagged for review.
• Assessment: Upon detection, the administrator assesses the scope and severity of the incident to determine if user data has been compromised.
• Containment: Immediate actions are taken to contain the incident, which may include revoking sessions, disabling compromised accounts, or temporarily restricting access.
• Notification: If a breach poses a real risk of significant harm, affected users, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec are notified as required by law.
• Recovery: Systems are restored to normal operation and additional safeguards are implemented to prevent recurrence.
• Documentation: All incidents are documented with a record of actions taken, findings, and remediation steps.
securityPolicy.section7Content:
BudgetWise integrates with Plaid Technologies, Inc. for bank account connectivity. The following security considerations apply:

• Plaid is SOC 2 Type II certified and maintains comprehensive security controls.
• BudgetWise communicates with Plaid exclusively through their secure API using encrypted connections.
• Plaid access tokens are stored server-side and are never exposed to the client application.
• Users can disconnect their bank connections at any time, which revokes the associated Plaid access tokens.
• BudgetWise supports both Plaid Sandbox and Production environments, with clear separation between test and live data.

No other third-party services have access to user financial data.
securityPolicy.section8Content:
Users have full control over their data within BudgetWise:

• Data Export: Users can export their financial data at any time in CSV or JSON format.
• Data Deletion: Users can securely delete all their financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and categorization rules) through the Settings page. This action requires password confirmation.
• Consent Management: Users can manage granular consent preferences for data collection, processing, and storage. Revoking consent triggers appropriate data handling actions.
• Account Security: Users can change their password, enable or disable two-factor authentication, and monitor their account activity through the audit log (administrators).

These controls ensure compliance with the right of access, rectification, deletion, and portability as required by PIPEDA and Quebec Law 25.
securityPolicy.section9Content:
This Information Security Policy is a living document and is subject to regular review:

• Annual Review: This policy is reviewed at least once per year to ensure it remains current and effective.
• Trigger-Based Updates: The policy is updated whenever there are significant changes to the application architecture, new regulatory requirements, or following a security incident.
• Version Control: All changes to this policy are tracked with a revision date. Previous versions are archived for reference.
• Approval: This policy is approved by the BudgetWise application owner. Any substantive changes require review and re-approval before taking effect.

The "Last updated" date at the top of this document reflects the most recent revision.
securityPolicy.section10Content:
BudgetWise is designed to comply with the following regulatory frameworks:

• Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA): Canada's federal private-sector privacy law.
• Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25): Quebec's provincial privacy legislation, including requirements for privacy impact assessments, incident reporting, and consent management.

This Information Security Policy, together with our Privacy Policy, forms the foundation of our compliance program. We are committed to adapting our practices as regulatory requirements evolve.
securityPolicy.section11Content:
BudgetWise maintains an active software lifecycle management program to ensure all components remain supported, patched, and secure. End-of-life (EOL) software no longer receives security updates or patches, making it vulnerable to exploitation.

Our EOL management practices include:

• Weekly Dependency Updates: All application dependencies (npm packages, libraries, frameworks) are reviewed and updated on a weekly basis to ensure known vulnerabilities are patched promptly.
• Server Software Monitoring: Core server components — including the operating system, Apache HTTP Server, PHP runtime, and MariaDB/MySQL database — are monitored for EOL announcements and upgraded before support ends.
• EOL Tracking: The administrator maintains awareness of end-of-life dates for all critical software components using vendor announcements and public EOL tracking resources (e.g., endoflife.date).
• Automated Vulnerability Scanning: Dependency security scans (e.g., npm audit, GitHub Dependabot) are used to detect known vulnerabilities in third-party packages. Critical and high-severity findings are addressed within one week.
• Replacement Planning: When a software component approaches its end-of-life date, a migration or replacement plan is established in advance to ensure a smooth transition without service disruption.
• Documentation: All software component versions, their EOL dates, and update actions are documented for audit and compliance purposes.

This proactive approach minimizes the risk of running unsupported software and ensures the continued security and stability of the BudgetWise platform.
securityPolicy.section12Content:
BudgetWise adopts zero trust principles to strengthen its security posture. Under a zero trust model, no user, device, or network is trusted by default — every access request is verified before being granted.

The following zero trust controls are implemented:

• Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Optional TOTP-based two-factor authentication is available for all users, providing a second layer of identity verification beyond passwords.
• Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Access is strictly segmented by role. Administrators and standard users have clearly defined, separate privilege levels. Standard users cannot access administrative functions or other users' data.
• Least Privilege: Users are granted only the minimum access necessary. API endpoints enforce user-scoped queries, preventing unauthorized data access at the application layer.
• Session Token Validation: Every API request is authenticated server-side using cryptographically generated session tokens with defined expiration periods. Tokens are validated against the database on each request.
• Continuous Monitoring: All authentication events — successful logins, failed login attempts, 2FA changes, password changes, and administrative actions — are logged in a comprehensive audit system. Administrators have access to a real-time Security Monitoring dashboard that tracks failed login patterns, identifies suspicious IP addresses, detects targeted account attacks, and provides an overall security health status with automated alerting.
• No Implicit Trust: There is no public self-registration. All user accounts are created by administrators, ensuring that only explicitly authorized individuals can access the system.
• Session Isolation: Authentication tokens are stored in session storage (not persistent storage), reducing the risk of token theft across browser sessions.

Future enhancements under consideration include device identity verification (trusted device management) and step-up authentication for sensitive operations (e.g., requiring re-authentication before changing security settings or deleting data).

This zero trust approach ensures that access is continuously verified and that the blast radius of any potential compromise is minimized.

accessControlPolicy.title: Access Control Policy
accessControlPolicy.contact: For questions regarding this Access Control Policy, please contact:
accessControlPolicy.section1Content:
This Access Control Policy establishes the principles, standards, and procedures governing access to BudgetWise information systems and data assets. The objective of this policy is to ensure that access to resources is granted on a need-to-know basis, consistent with the principle of least privilege, and that all access is appropriately authorized, monitored, and revoked when no longer required.

This policy supports the objectives of BudgetWise's Information Security Policy and Privacy Policy by ensuring that only authorized individuals can access sensitive information, thereby protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of user data.
accessControlPolicy.section2Content:
This policy applies to:

• All users of the BudgetWise application, including administrators and standard users.
• All information assets managed by the application, including user accounts, financial data, bank connections, budgets, categorization rules, and audit logs.
• All access methods, including web-based application access, API access, and database access.
• All environments: production, staging, and development.

This policy covers both logical access (application and database level) and administrative access (system configuration and user management).
accessControlPolicy.section3Content:
BudgetWise enforces the principle of least privilege across all access controls:

• Users are granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their intended functions within the application.
• Standard users can access only their own financial data — transactions, accounts, budgets, and reports. They cannot view or modify other users' data.
• Administrative privileges are reserved for designated administrators and are not granted by default.
• API endpoints enforce user-scoped queries, ensuring data isolation at the application layer.
• Access to sensitive system settings (Plaid credentials, backend configuration) is restricted exclusively to administrators.

Access rights are reviewed whenever a user's role changes to ensure they remain appropriate.
accessControlPolicy.section4Content:
BudgetWise implements a role-based access control model with two defined roles:

• Administrator: Full access to all application features, including user management (create, edit, delete users), Plaid API configuration, backend setup and diagnostics, audit log review, and all standard user features. Administrators are accountable for the responsible use of their elevated privileges.
• Standard User: Access to personal financial features including dashboard, transactions, budgets, reports, accounts, bank connections, and personal settings. Standard users can manage their own security settings (password, two-factor authentication) and consent preferences.

Additional access permissions:
• Sandbox Access: By default, standard users are restricted to the Production Plaid environment. Administrators may grant individual users access to the Sandbox environment on a per-user basis for testing purposes.

Role assignments are managed exclusively by administrators through the user management interface.
accessControlPolicy.section5Content:
Access to BudgetWise is granted through the following controlled procedures:

• Account Creation: New user accounts are created exclusively by administrators. There is no public self-registration. Administrators specify the user's name, email, password, role, and sandbox access permission at creation time.
• Password Requirements: Passwords must be a minimum of 6 characters. Users are encouraged to use strong, unique passwords. All passwords are hashed using bcrypt before storage.
• Initial Access: Upon account creation, users receive their credentials from the administrator and should change their password upon first login.
• Two-Factor Authentication: Users are strongly encouraged to enable TOTP-based two-factor authentication for an additional layer of security. 2FA can be configured in the user's personal Settings.

All account creation events are recorded in the audit log.
accessControlPolicy.section6Content:
Changes to user access are managed through defined procedures:

• Role Changes: Administrators can modify a user's role (standard user to administrator, or vice versa) through the user management interface. Role changes take effect immediately.
• Sandbox Access: Administrators can grant or revoke sandbox environment access for individual standard users at any time.
• Profile Updates: Administrators can update a user's name, email, and password. Users can also change their own password and manage their 2FA settings.
• Consent Changes: Users can modify their data consent preferences (collection, processing, storage) at any time through Privacy & Consent settings. Changes to consent may affect the user's ability to use certain features.

All access modifications are logged in the audit system with timestamps and the identity of the administrator who made the change.
accessControlPolicy.section7Content:
Access is revoked promptly when no longer required:

• Account Deletion: Administrators can delete user accounts through the user management interface. Account deletion requires confirmation and permanently removes the user's access.
• Session Termination: Users can log out to terminate their active session. Authentication tokens are invalidated upon logout.
• Data Deletion: Users can request the deletion of all their financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and categorization rules) through the Settings page. This action requires password confirmation.
• Bank Connection Removal: Users can disconnect their bank connections at any time, which revokes the associated Plaid access tokens and prevents further data synchronization.
• Consent Withdrawal: Revoking data storage consent triggers a secure deletion process for all stored financial data.

All access revocation events are recorded in the audit log for accountability.
accessControlPolicy.section8Content:
BudgetWise implements the following authentication controls to verify user identity:

• Password Authentication: Primary authentication using email and password. Passwords are hashed using bcrypt and never stored in plain text.
• Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): Optional TOTP-based second factor using an authenticator app. Recovery codes are provided during setup for account recovery.
• Session Tokens: Cryptographically generated authentication tokens with defined expiration periods. Tokens are stored in session storage and validated server-side against the auth_tokens database table.
• Failed Login Monitoring: Authentication failures are recorded in the audit log, enabling administrators to detect and respond to potential brute-force attacks.

These controls work together to provide defense-in-depth against unauthorized access.
accessControlPolicy.section9Content:
Access to BudgetWise systems is monitored through a comprehensive audit logging system:

• All authentication events are logged: successful logins, failed login attempts, logouts, 2FA enablement and disablement, and password changes.
• Administrative actions are logged: user creation, user updates, user deletion, and configuration changes.
• Each audit log entry includes: timestamp, user identity, action type, IP address, and user agent information.
• Administrators can review the audit log through a dedicated interface to identify anomalies or unauthorized access attempts.

Audit logs are retained in accordance with applicable legal requirements and are protected against unauthorized modification.
accessControlPolicy.section10Content:
This Access Control Policy is maintained as a living document:

• Annual Review: This policy is reviewed at least once per year to ensure it reflects current access control practices and security requirements.
• Trigger-Based Updates: The policy is updated whenever there are significant changes to the application's role model, authentication mechanisms, or regulatory requirements.
• Alignment: This policy is maintained in alignment with BudgetWise's Information Security Policy and Privacy Policy.
• Approval: Changes to this policy require review and approval by the BudgetWise application owner.
• Version Control: All revisions are tracked with a revision date. The "Last updated" date at the top of this document reflects the most recent revision.

Users and administrators are expected to familiarize themselves with this policy and adhere to its provisions.

dataRetentionPolicy.title: Data Retention and Deletion Policy
dataRetentionPolicy.contact: For questions regarding this Data Retention and Deletion Policy, please contact:
dataRetentionPolicy.section1Content:
This Data Retention and Deletion Policy establishes the principles, standards, and procedures governing the retention, archival, and secure deletion of data within BudgetWise. The objective of this policy is to ensure that data is retained only for as long as necessary to fulfill its intended purpose, comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and minimize the risks associated with unnecessary data retention.

This policy supports BudgetWise's commitment to data minimization and user privacy as outlined in our Privacy Policy, Information Security Policy, and Access Control Policy, and ensures compliance with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) and Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25).
dataRetentionPolicy.section2Content:
This policy applies to all data collected, processed, and stored by the BudgetWise application, including:

• User account data: names, email addresses, hashed passwords, role assignments, and authentication settings.
• Financial data: bank account information, transaction records, budget configurations, category assignments, and categorization rules.
• Connection data: Plaid integration tokens, bank connection metadata, and synchronization cursors.
• Audit data: authentication events, administrative actions, security events, IP addresses, and user agent information.
• Consent records: user consent preferences for data collection, processing, and storage.
• Session data: authentication tokens and session metadata.

This policy applies to data in all environments (production, staging, and development) and in all states (at rest, in transit, and in processing).
dataRetentionPolicy.section3Content:
BudgetWise's data retention practices are governed by the following regulatory frameworks:

• Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA): Requires that personal information be retained only as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected. Organizations must establish and document retention periods.
• Quebec's Law 25 (Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector): Requires organizations to destroy personal information once the purpose for which it was collected has been achieved, unless the individual consents to longer retention or a law requires it.
• Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requirements: Financial records that may be relevant for tax purposes should be retained for a minimum of six (6) years from the end of the last tax year to which they relate.

Where legal requirements conflict, the longer retention period applies. Where no specific legal requirement exists, data is retained only as long as reasonably necessary for its intended purpose.
dataRetentionPolicy.section4Content:
The following retention periods apply to data within BudgetWise:

• Financial transaction data: Retained for the duration of the user's active account plus six (6) years following account closure or data deletion request, to comply with CRA record-keeping requirements. Users may request earlier deletion of their data, but should be advised of potential tax compliance implications.
• Bank account and connection data: Retained for the duration of the active connection. Upon disconnection by the user, Plaid access tokens are immediately revoked and connection metadata is deleted.
• Budget and categorization data: Retained for the duration of the user's active account. Deleted immediately upon user request.
• User account data: Retained for the duration of the active account. Upon account deletion by an administrator, all associated data is permanently removed.
• Audit log entries: Retained for a minimum of three (3) years to support security reviews, incident investigations, and regulatory compliance. Audit logs are protected against unauthorized modification.
• Session and authentication tokens: Automatically expired according to defined session timeout periods. Expired tokens are purged during routine maintenance.
• Consent records: Retained for the duration of the user's active account plus two (2) years following account closure, to demonstrate compliance with consent requirements under PIPEDA and Law 25.
dataRetentionPolicy.section5Content:
BudgetWise provides users with the ability to securely delete their financial data at any time:

• Data Deletion Request: Users can initiate deletion of all their financial data (transactions, accounts, connections, budgets, and categorization rules) through the Settings page under Privacy & Consent.
• Verification: Data deletion requires the user to type "DELETE" as confirmation and enter their account password. This dual confirmation prevents accidental data loss.
• Scope of Deletion: The deletion process removes all user-associated financial data in a single atomic transaction, ensuring data consistency. Specifically, the following are deleted: transaction splits, transactions, accounts, Plaid connections, budgets, category rules, and user categories.
• Immediacy: Deletion is performed immediately upon confirmation. There is no grace period or recovery option once deletion is confirmed.
• Audit Trail: The data deletion event is recorded in the audit log for compliance purposes. The audit log entry does not contain the deleted data itself.
• Consent Reset: Upon successful deletion, the user's data storage consent preference is automatically reset.

Users are advised to export their data before requesting deletion if they wish to retain a personal copy.
dataRetentionPolicy.section6Content:
Administrators have the ability to manage user data through the following procedures:

• Account Deletion: Administrators can delete user accounts through the user management interface. Account deletion permanently removes the user and all associated data, including financial records, connections, and settings.
• Cascading Deletion: When a user account is deleted, all related records across all tables are removed through cascading foreign key constraints, ensuring no orphaned data remains.
• Audit Record: All administrative deletion actions are logged in the audit system with the administrator's identity, timestamp, and the affected user's information.

Administrators are trained to exercise caution when deleting user data and to confirm the action before proceeding.
dataRetentionPolicy.section7Content:
BudgetWise employs the following methods to ensure data is securely and irreversibly deleted:

• Database Deletion: Data is deleted from the MySQL/MariaDB database using SQL DELETE operations within transactions. Once committed, the data is no longer accessible through the application or database queries.
• Plaid Token Revocation: When bank connections are removed, the associated Plaid access tokens are revoked through the Plaid API, preventing any further access to the user's bank data.
• Session Invalidation: Authentication tokens are invalidated by deletion from the auth_tokens table, immediately terminating any active sessions.
• No Soft Deletes: BudgetWise does not implement soft-delete patterns. When data is deleted, it is permanently removed from the database, not merely flagged as inactive.
• Backup Considerations: If database backups are maintained, retention of backups follows the same retention schedule as the data they contain. Backups older than the applicable retention period are securely destroyed.
dataRetentionPolicy.section8Content:
The following automated mechanisms support retention policy enforcement:

• Session Expiration: Authentication tokens have defined expiration periods. Expired tokens are automatically invalidated and no longer grant access.
• Connection Cleanup: When a user disconnects a bank connection, all associated tokens and metadata are immediately removed.
• Consent-Driven Deletion: When a user revokes data storage consent, the system initiates a secure deletion workflow that removes all stored financial data.

Future enhancements may include automated purging of expired audit log entries and periodic review reminders for data that has exceeded its retention period.
dataRetentionPolicy.section9Content:
Data may be retained beyond its standard retention period in the following circumstances:

• Legal Hold: If BudgetWise receives a legal order or is involved in litigation, relevant data may be preserved beyond its normal retention period until the legal matter is resolved.
• Regulatory Investigation: If a regulatory body requests access to records, relevant data will be retained until the investigation is concluded.
• Active Disputes: If a user has an active complaint or dispute, their data will be retained until the matter is resolved.

In all cases, data retained under an exception is clearly identified and reviewed periodically to determine if continued retention is necessary. Once the exception no longer applies, the data is deleted according to standard procedures.
dataRetentionPolicy.section10Content:
This Data Retention and Deletion Policy is maintained as a living document:

• Annual Review: This policy is reviewed at least once per year to ensure it reflects current data handling practices, legal requirements, and application capabilities.
• Trigger-Based Updates: The policy is updated whenever there are significant changes to data collection practices, new regulatory requirements, or changes to the application's data architecture.
• Alignment: This policy is maintained in alignment with BudgetWise's Privacy Policy, Information Security Policy, and Access Control Policy.
• Approval: Changes to this policy require review and approval by the BudgetWise application owner.
• Version Control: All revisions are tracked with a revision date. The "Last updated" date at the top of this document reflects the most recent revision.

Users and administrators are expected to familiarize themselves with this policy and adhere to its provisions.
